newsitem.title: USA: U.S. not objecting to Turkish buffer zone in Iraq.
newsitem.headline: U.S. not objecting to Turkish buffer zone in Iraq.

text.p: The United States said on Thursday it was not objecting to Turkey's planned creation of a security zone in northern Iraq after Ankara said it would be short-lived and not involve the stationing of Turkish troops.
"We've taken note of it and we're not raising any particular objections based on what the Turks have told us," State Department spokesman Glyn Davies said.

"There's no great concern at this stage based on what we know and what we've been told that the Turkish action is going to be in any way destabilising in a larger sense in northern Iraq," Davies told a news briefing.
Turkish officials said on Wednesday Turkey was preparing to set up a security cordon inside northern Iraq to halt infiltration by PKK Kurdish guerrillas.

A foreign ministry official said the zone would be five to 10 km (three to six miles) deep. Its establishment follows a move by Iraqi troops into the Western-protected Kurdish region in northern Iraq, which prompted two U.S. cruise missile strikes on Iraq this week.
Turkey staged heavy military activity near its frontier with Iraq on Thursday, but Foreign Minister Tansu Ciller said a thrust across the border was not imminent.
"The Turkish government has assured us that no troops will be stationed in Iraq and that the zone will be temporary," Davies said.
"And as we've said repeatedly, we recognise the right of Turkey to defend itself against terrorism emanating from the PKK."
Davies agreed with a questioner that "presumably" Turkish troops would enter the security zone when required, but would not stay there.
